title: Ecosystems and Food Webs
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Ecosystems and Food Webs Worksheets (Interdependence, Bioaccumulation)
standard_code: KS3 Biology: Relationships in an ecosystem
standard_text: The interdependence of organisms in an ecosystem, including food webs and insect pollinated crops; the importance of plant reproduction through insect pollination in human food security; how organisms affect, and are affected by, their environment, including the accumulation of toxic materials.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on ecosystems: food chains and webs, energy transfer, interdependence, populations, pollinators and the build-up of poisons in food chains. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things in an ecosystem depend on each other.
key_sub: Energy flows along food chains; poisons build up at the top.
body_html:
How to think about it

In an ecosystem, living things depend on each other.

  • Food chains start with a producer; arrows show the flow of energy (what is eaten → what eats it).
  • Only about a tenth of the energy passes on at each level, so there are fewer animals higher up.
  • Poisons such as DDT build up along food chains, so top predators are harmed most.
Example

Grass → rabbit → fox: rabbits removed. Foxes?

Less food for foxes

Answer: decrease

Example

1,000 units in grass, 10% passed on. Rabbits get?

1,000 × 0.1

Answer: 100 units

Common mistakes

  • Drawing arrows towards what is eaten.
  • Thinking energy is recycled.
  • Thinking poison is diluted up a food chain.

faq.q: Which way do food chain arrows point?
faq.a: From the organism that is eaten to the one that eats it, showing the direction energy flows.
The build-up of a poison such as DDT or mercury along a food chain. Each animal eats many of the one below, so top predators get the highest concentration.

faq.q: Why do insect pollinators matter for food?
faq.a: Many crops, such as apples and strawberries, need insects to carry pollen between flowers so that fruits and seeds can form.
